changelog: Insert a short binding that keeps a noun head with any immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier (restrictive relative clause, appositive, title/multiword name, or prepositional complement) so cuts do not separate a noun from the modifier that identifies or restricts it — addresses the primary finding about cohesion loss.
findings: The prompt routinely treats a pre-verbal fragment as self-contained and allows cuts immediately before a clause’s main finite verb or copula, leaving the preceding piece without its predicate and producing high-contradiction/low-cohesion outputs.

The prompt allows cuts that split a noun head from an essential post‑nominal modifier (appositive, restrictive 'which/that' clause, prepositional complement, title or multiword name), underestimating the cohesion loss when the modifier defines or identifies the noun.

edits.now: - Keep a noun head together with any immediately following essential post‑nomina

diagnosis.why: The inserted binding (keep a noun head with any immediately following essential post‑nominal modifier) caused the model to avoid cuts that would split a head+modifier, so it often moved cuts earlier (placing the cut before the noun) to keep the noun+modifier together. That change helps very short pieces and list/title splits (bins ≤3/≤5, best examples) but harms longer, multi‑clause sentences (overall ≤99 negative and a big drop in rank for k=1) by fragmenting adjacent clauses and moving cuts into preceding material.
diagnosis.lesson: When adding a noun‑head+modifier binding, ensure it does not force earlier cuts that fragment adjacent clauses or long spans — only apply it when it can be satisfied without shifting cuts into preceding material.
